query: For a multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy exposed to simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature, what single mechanistic hypothesis could explain the accelerated coupled degradation and why it occurs? Specify a controlled comparison capable of distinguishing the proposed explanation, predict the changes in total degradation and the individual wear and corrosion responses relative to a matched baseline, define the relevant boundary conditions, identify supporting evidence, and give a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: In a eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) that contains alternating FCC (NiCoFeCr) and Cr/Mn-rich intermetallic lamellae, the large electrochemical potential difference between the two phases generates micro-galvanic cells at elevated temperature. Preferential anodic dissolution of the Cr/Mn-rich phase (structural mediator) produces a porous, mechanically soft surface oxide. Sliding contact then removes this weakened layer more easily than the intact matrix and simultaneously exposes fresh metal, keeping the galvanic couple active. The feedback between (i) corrosion-induced micro-porosity/softening and (ii) wear-induced oxide removal accelerates both wear and corrosion beyond their simple sum.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast, lamellar eutectic high-entropy alloy (e.g., (NiCoFeCr) FCC + Cr/Mn-rich BCC intermetallic, ~50–150 nm lamellar spacing).
generation.intervention: Homogenisation heat treatment at 1150 °C for 24 h followed by water quench to convert the lamellar eutectic into a single-phase FCC solid solution (eliminates micro-galvanic phase contrast).
generation.conditions: Sliding wear: alumina counter-pin, 5 N load, 0.1 m s⁻¹ sliding speed, 30 min. Corrosive medium: 0.1 M Na2SO4 + 0.01 M H2SO4 at 400 °C under flowing O2/steam mixture (0.2 atm pO2, 10 % H2O).
generation.structural_mediator: Cr/Mn-rich interdendritic lamellar phase acting as local anode, creating a porous oxide skeleton after selective dissolution.
generation.mechanism:
1. At 400 °C the electrochemical potential gap drives rapid selective dissolution of Cr/Mn-rich lamellae.
2. Resulting porous oxide layer has ~30 % lower hardness than bulk FCC matrix.
3. Sliding removes the porous layer, lowering the effective oxide thickness (<1 µm) and exposing fresh metal.
4. Newly exposed lamellae corrode again, sustaining the cycle.
5. The coupled process therefore produces super-additive total mass loss (wear + corrosion) compared to the linear sum of the two processes acting separately.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the homogenised single-phase control: (a) Total mass loss of the lamellar EHEA under simultaneous wear/corrosion will be ≥50 % higher than the arithmetic sum of (wear-only loss + corrosion-only loss); (b) Wear volume will be ~2× higher and electrochemical current density ~3× higher than those of the control under the same coupled test.
generation.baseline: Homogenised single-phase EHEA tested under identical mechanical and environmental conditions but without galvanic phase contrast; expected to show near-additive behaviour (total loss within ±10 % of the sum of isolated wear and corrosion losses).
generation.boundary: Valid for 300–500 °C, aqueous sulfate environments with pO2 ≥0.1 atm, sliding contact pressures 1–10 N, and lamellar spacing ≤500 nm. Outside this window (e.g., ≤200 °C or fully protective chromia scales) the synergy is expected to diminish.
generation.uncertainty: No direct quantitative data yet link lamellar dissolution rates to hardness loss at 400 °C; magnitude estimates (≥50 % synergy, 2–3× individual responses) are therefore uncertain by ±30 %.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two specimens: (i) as-cast lamellar EHEA, (ii) homogenised single-phase EHEA. Measure: (1) open-circuit corrosion current and oxide thickness under no sliding; (2) wear volume under inert gas; (3) total mass loss, real-time corrosion current, and post-test surface morphology during simultaneous wear + corrosion as per conditions above.
measurements: Mass/volume loss by precision weighing and profilometry
Nano-indentation hardness of the oxide layer
Cross-sectional SEM/EDS to quantify lamellar dissolution depth
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the lamellar EHEA shows (a) total coupled loss that is ≤10 % greater than the sum of its isolated wear and corrosion losses OR (b) coupled wear and corrosion rates within ±15 % of the single-phase control, then the hypothesis of galvanically driven porous-oxide-mediated synergy is falsified.
